module.name: Regime Blindness Checklist
module.purpose: Minimal diagnostic bridge for researchers entering RTT/vST-aware work — identifies Regime Blindness, the structural failure mode that occurs when researchers evaluate a new conceptual substrate using the grammar, metrics, or assumptions of an old one.

files.purpose: Navigation index for the Regime Blindness Checklist — introduces the diagnostic purpose, file sequence, usage instructions, and intended audience.
Formal definition of Regime Blindness — the structural inability to recognize that a system has shifted into a new regime with different invariants, metrics, and coherence rules.
Diagnostic catalog of common Regime Blindness indicators across disciplines — misapplied observer frames, legacy metric misreads, and contradiction-as-noise patterns.
Quick triadic diagnostic tool for active researcher self-assessment — structured checklist for detecting regime mismatch in current projects, models, or interpretations.
Diagnostic reference explaining how outdated metrics distort interpretation when observer frames remain locked to a prior regime.
Reference for identifying topology shifts in conceptual systems — boundary markers where one structural regime ends and another begins.
Worked examples of real-world regime mismatch — concrete cases where Regime Blindness produced misinterpretations, contradictions, or stalled progress.
Operator-facing corrective action steps for re-anchoring the observer frame to the correct regime — active re-alignment procedures for researchers.
Citation reference linking to the canonical DOI for the Regime Blindness Checklist as a citable research artifact.
